item.title: 'No problem': Trump backs release of alleged drug boat strike footage; repeats warning of land strikes in Venezuela
item.description: President Trump stated he would support the release of footage from strikes on an alleged Venezuelan drug boat, backing the "decision to knock out the boats." He suggested the situation is "war" due to drug smuggling's impact. Trump also reiterated threats of imminent land strikes in Venezuela.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Watch: US Thunderbirds F-16 erupts in flames near Trona Airport; video shows pilot drifting by parachute
item.description: A US Air Force F-16 fighter jet from the elite Thunderbirds demonstration team crashed during a training flight in Southern California. The pilot ejected safely and is receiving medical treatment. The cause of the incident, which occurred near Trona Airport, is currently unknown. The Thunderbirds are known for their thrilling, high-precision aerial displays.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Hegseth risked US troops by sharing strike details on Signal, Pentagon watchdog finds
item.description: US Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth faces scrutiny over using the Signal app for sensitive military strike details, including minute-by-minute updates on a Houthi operation. The Pentagon's watchdog found he violated policy by using a personal device, though the review didn't conclude classified material was mishandled. Critics argue this jeopardized troop safety.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Declared dead, woman suddenly wakes up in mortuary: Paramedic blunder or tragic error?
item.description: In October 2023, Darlington resident Olive Martin suffered a seizure at home and was mistakenly declared dead by paramedics, who transported her to a hospital mortuary instead of A&E. Mortuary staff discovered she was still alive, but she later died from brain damage. A coroner’s inquest is now examining whether crucial treatment time was lost—and whether her life might have been saved.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: MrBeast becomes the top US YouTuber for the sixth year in a row
item.description: MrBeast has been named the top YouTube creator in the U.S. for the sixth consecutive year in 2025. With over 453 million subscribers, his channel continues to dominate through high-budget, engaging content and philanthropic stunts. His innovative approach and massive viewership solidify his position as the highest-paid YouTuber and a defining figure in online entertainment.

item.title: Drunk raccoon breaks into liquor store, downs scotch, and passes out in bathroom
item.description: In Ashland, Virginia, staff at a liquor store arrived to find smashed whisky bottles and a raccoon passed out in the bathroom after falling through the ceiling and drinking freely from the stock. Animal control officer Samantha Martin confirmed the “suspect” was extremely intoxicated. After sobering up, the raccoon was released back into the wild, hungover, unharmed, and hopefully wiser.

item.title: “Be lucky or know the right people”: Emiru on why Twitch growth is difficult
item.description: Streamer Emiru shared that growing on Twitch is significantly harder than on platforms like TikTok and Instagram. She believes success on Twitch often hinges on luck or knowing the right people, due to its top-heavy structure and poor discoverability. This sentiment resonates with many smaller creators struggling to gain visibility.

item.title: xQc opens up about the off-camera version of MrBeast that doesn’t appear in videos
item.description: YouTuber xQc shared insights into MrBeast's personality. He noted that MrBeast appears more genuine and relaxed when not filming. xQc explained that MrBeast adopts a different on-camera style to suit YouTube's demands. This adjustment is necessary to avoid backlash on the platform. MrBeast himself has indicated a shift towards more story-driven content.

item.title: Wendy Ortiz apologizes after calling Stable Ronaldo a “woman hater”
item.description: Streamer Wendy Ortiz retracted her "woman hater" accusations against FaZe Clan's Stable Ronaldo and Jasontheween following intense backlash. Initially defending Nina Lin, Ortiz's live comments sparked widespread criticism. Despite her subsequent claims of affection for the FaZe members, the incident highlights the rapid escalation of online disputes and the impact of public statements.

item.title: Who is Nicholas Hunter? The YouTuber behind the viral fake pregnancy story with Jade and her mother Dani
item.description: South Florida YouTuber Nick Yardy, known for comedy, sparked widespread shock with a fabricated pregnancy announcement involving a 22-year-old creator and her 44-year-old mother. Despite the elaborate hoax, which fooled millions and garnered media attention, Yardy later admitted it was a skit for views. He claims his relationship with both women remains real.
item.dc:creator: Global Sports Desk

item.title: 'Dear god, make it stop:' Home Alone house owner reveals decades of intrusion in new memoir
item.description: Former Home Alone homeowner John Abendshien reveals how his idyllic suburban life was upended by the movie’s fame. What began as a fun filming opportunity turned into decades of lost privacy, gawking tourists and strangers treating his front lawn as nostalgic property. His account shows the hidden cost of cultural landmarking, and what it means when the world decides your house belongs to them.

item.title: ‘Sleepy Joe’ to ‘Sleepy Trump’: How Donald Trump dozed off in a meeting after years of mocking Biden
item.description: Cameras captured Donald Trump appearing to doze during a Cabinet meeting, sparking the "Sleepy Trump" meme and a debate about his alertness. This incident, occurring twice in a month, clashes with his "low energy" attacks on rivals and fuels scrutiny of his age and stamina, despite White House claims of his full engagement.
